text: 1295. Khāśi. metrër, metrelā ‘stepmother’ < OIA *mātr̥tarā- ‘stepmother’ (10022); regarding Srk. matərma ‘stepmother’, Jaṭ. matrˈimā ‘stepmother’ and Maṇḍ. māhtimī ‘woman’ cf. RV mātŕ̥tama- ‘very like a mother’. The Khāśi. form is remarkable for preservation of the syllabic -r̥-, and the lemma is remarkable for its closeness to Lat. matertera ‘maternal aunt’ and (slightly less close) Gr. 𝜇𝜂𝜏𝜌𝜐𝜄𝛼́ ‘stepmother’ (see IGN: 80 and Martrirosyan [2013: 112]). Cf. also Brah. mātuna ‘stepmother’, Arm. mawrvi ‘of a stepmother’ (Mann [1963: 39]) or mauru ‘stepmother’ (IGN: 80) and Psht. maira ‘stepmother’ for which Morgenstierne, however, reconstructs Av. *māθryā-. Still, note also that there are several NIA languages with similar sounding words, however with meaning ‘mother’, e.g. Aw. mahᵃtārī.

text: 959. Bng. pãsrɔ ‘lethargic, listless’ and pãsru adj.;n.m. ‘lethargic, listless; dustweb, thread hanging on cloth, ribbon’ derive < OIA pāṁśurá- ‘dusty’ (8021) (Pk.) and are, despite many modern parallels, worth quoting here because Bng. has preserved the old form with -s- (and not -ś-) and -r- (and not -l-) and has a partially different meaning. With the Bng. form comparable is also Pr. pərċˈə ‘dust’ which Buddruss und Degener associate with OIA pāṁśu-, pāṁsú- ‘crumbling soil, dust, sand’ (8019) but point out that for Turner the -r- is inexplicable. Probably quite closely related with Pr. appears Kann. pŭrcūṭiṅ ‘dust’ (with a suffix?). Mayrhofer (EWA) rejects Lienhard’s suggestion to interpret OIA pāṁsú- as an MIA development < *prāṁśu- but he does not consider the Pr. and Kann. forms. The origin of the lemma is unclear, but the Pr. form does not reflect a Proto-IA stage because from Niya Pk. the change of ṁs > ċ is known as e.g. in saṁsāra- > saċara- (see e.g. T. Burrow [1937: 18f.]).
